To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
DMSO, dimethylformamide (DMF), dimethylacetamide (DMA), ethanol, and methanole all reduce rat liver N-acetylatransferase (NAT II) activity in vitro.
dimethylsulfoxides (DMSO) and several other organic solvents can inhibit rat liver cytosol acetyl CoA:N-acetyl transferase activity.
dimethylsulfoxidemethanol, dimethylformamide and ethanol inhibit rat liver cytosol acetyl CoA:N-acetyltransferase isozymes in vitro.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of solvents on the acetyl CoA-dependent acetylation of aromatic amines by rat liver cytosol.
the effects of solvents on the activity of rat liver cytosol acetyl CoA:N-acetyltransferase.
the effect of various solvents on the activity of rat liver cytosol NAT isozymes.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
DMSO, dimethylformamide and dimethylacetamide should be used with caution in studies involving NAT.
DMSO should be avoided as a solubilizing agent for in vitro studies of arylamine metabolism, particularly when NAT II is being investigated, and that DMSO may inhibit arylamine metabolism in vivo.
DMSO inhibits NAT II competitively and that the inhibitory activity of other solvents may be similar to that of DMSO.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the solvents tested in the present study are not suitable for the in vitro study of NAT II.
DMSO, dimethylformamide and dimethylacetamide should be avoided as solubilizing agents in in vitro assays for NAT II activity.
the use of DMSO in in vitro NAT assays should be avoided.
The main takeaway from our work is that
DMSO should not be used in studies of arylamine metabolism in vitro.
solvents used to dissolve substrates for NAT in vitro may have a significant effect on the measured activity of NAT in vitro.
the solvents used in the in vitro NAT assay should be considered when comparing results from different labs and when interpreting the results of NAT activity assays.
